items.headline: FBI probes apparent hack of national crime database
items.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center, the database police use to check fugitives, missing persons and criminal histories, according to an AP source. The breach comes amid a string of U.S. tech disruptions.

items.headline: Trump tells contractors to clear answers to Congress
items.summary: President Trump ordered federal contractors to check with the White House before responding to Congress. The move is the latest effort to resist expected Democratic oversight once Democrats take control of Congress in January.

items.headline: Mexico arrests cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro'
items.summary: Mexican authorities detained Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a Beltrán Leyva cartel leader once on the FBI's 10 most wanted list. The arrest set off a burst of violence in Sinaloa.

items.headline: Ebola death toll passes 5,700
items.summary: The death toll from the current Ebola outbreak has topped 5,700. Health officials face questions about whether the outbreak can be contained.

items.headline: U.N. talks fail to set binding rules on 'killer robots'
items.summary: U.N.-backed talks in Geneva on autonomous weapons ended with an agreement to keep talking for two more years but no firm commitments to restrict them. Humanitarian groups say military AI is advancing faster than diplomacy.

items.headline: Coastal storms threaten Thanksgiving travel
items.summary: Storms expected on both the Pacific and Atlantic coasts could disrupt Thanksgiving travel this week. San Francisco's mayor asked residents not to travel unless it is essential.

items.headline: Trump backs 10% cap on credit card interest
items.summary: President Trump said he will work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%. The median card rate is about 22.2%, according to a New York Fed survey.

items.headline: Bessent rules out new limits on Nvidia chips to China
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said no further restrictions are needed on Nvidia chip exports to China. He said the proper limits are in place and remote access has been curtailed.

items.headline: Rubio and Vance join Trump at briefing
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice President JD Vance joined President Trump for a White House briefing. The appearance was the latest in what PBS describes as a public audition of potential successors.

items.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-aided breakthrough
items.summary: An Anthropic mathematician says he solved a famous unsolved math problem with help from the company's Claude AI tool. It is the second such recent claim by a party tied to AI.

digest.overview:
The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center, the database police rely on for fugitive and criminal-history checks. President Trump ordered federal contractors to consult the White House before answering Congress, bracing for Democratic oversight in January. Trump also said he would work with Democrats to cap credit card interest at 10%, far below the roughly 22% median rate. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said no new limits are needed on Nvidia chip sales to China. Marco Rubio and JD Vance joined Trump at a White House briefing seen as a showcase for possible successors. Storms on both coasts threaten Thanksgiving travel, and San Francisco's mayor urged residents to stay home unless trips are essential. Texas said an execution went as planned, though a witness described screams of distress. An Anthropic mathematician claimed he solved a famous open math problem with help from the company's AI.

Abroad, Mexico arrested Beltrán Leyva cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," setting off violence in Sinaloa. The Financial Times reported that Trump wants a Ukraine peace deal before Democrats take the House on Jan. 3, with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner shuttling among Moscow, Dublin and Berlin. Axios reported the two met senior Qatari officials in Berlin about reviving U.S.-Iran talks, which the White House did not confirm. The Ebola outbreak's death toll has passed 5,700. U.N.-backed talks in Geneva on autonomous weapons ended with a two-year extension of discussions but no binding limits.

home.overview:
Victor Wembanyama poured in 50 points with 19 rebounds as the Spurs routed the Pelicans 114–91, while Tyler Herro's career-high 50 wasn't enough for Milwaukee in a 132–129 loss at Philadelphia. The Knicks blew a 26-point lead before edging Portland 97–96 on a buzzer-beater, and lowly Sacramento stunned shorthanded Boston by the same score for its first home win. Minnesota and Dallas also won, and seven NBA games follow today. NFL Week 11 resumes with 10 afternoon games before Vikings–49ers in Mexico City; Arizona turns to Josh Johnson, its fourth starter in four weeks. In baseball, the Mets reportedly locked up A.J. Ewing for eight years and $95 million as the Dec. 1 labor deadline nears.

Arsenal were held 2–2 at Newcastle but still lead the Premier League by six points, Leeds won 4–1 at Chelsea, and Pochettino's Man United era starts at Anfield today. Dortmund won at Gladbach to go top of the Bundesliga, Real Madrid drew level with Barcelona, and PSG won a five-goal thriller at Nice. Middlesbrough top the Championship, Columbus won 3–0 at Inter Miami in MLS, and Suwon FC sealed promotion from K League 2. In the KBO, SSG re-signed reliever Moon Seung-won.

fact.answer:
Bread starts going stale as soon as the loaf leaves the oven and cools. The main cause is starch retrogradation: starch molecules crystallize, drawing water away from the gluten, and the crumb's network turns rigid at room temperature and below.

A common misconception is that stale bread has simply dried out. Britannica notes that texture staling can happen without any appreciable loss of moisture; drying produces a similar feel but is a separate effect. Food scientists say the process is still not fully understood.

Heat partly reverses the change. Warming stale bread to about 60–65°C (140–150°F), or toasting it, softens the crumb, though it ends up gummier than fresh bread and can dry out if overheated. Commercial bakers add ingredients such as monoglycerides to slow staling.
fact.question: Why does bread go stale?
